risk_if_not_implemented: Without AI & Autonomous Technologies Output Filtering, AI and autonomous systems may produce unreliable, biased or unsafe outputs, act outside authorized scope, or expose sensitive data. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Harm from Illegal, Abusive or Unsafe Content / Conduct (R-GV-8), AI Output / Decision Integrity Failure (R-AI-1), Unintended or Unsafe Technology Behavior (R-AI-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10), Artificial Intelligence & Autonomous Technologies (AAT) System Failure or Unintended Behavior (MT-13), Adversarial Artificial Intelligence (AI) Attack (MT-29).

compensating_control_1.name: Data Loss Prevention (DLP)
compensating_control_1.description: Automated mechanisms exist to implement Data Loss Prevention (DLP) to protect sensitive information as it is stored, transmitted and processed.
compensating_control_1.justification: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) (DCH-40) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of AI & Autonomous Technologies Output Filtering (AAT-17.1) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Malicious Code Protection (Antimalware)
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize antimalware, or similar technologies, to detect and eradicate malicious code.
compensating_control_2.justification: Malicious Code Protection (Antimalware) (END-04) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of AI & Autonomous Technologies Output Filtering (AAT-17.1) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
